clue.text: Make offer to host Group E in Split

indicators.note: to host is to hold a guest inside, so the bidding word wraps round the group and the E

parts.note: to make an offer at auction is to bid
a sect is a religious group

explanation.surface: An auction where someone puts in a bid for a lot in the Group E section of a divided sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Something split down the middle has been cut into two halves, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Great many on satellite channel in centre

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
Io is a moon of Jupiter

indicators.note: in centre picks out the single middle letter of the word channel

explanation.surface: A huge audience is watching some satellite channel at the heart of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket convention that on side equals leg side supplies the first three letters; cricket's leg side is the half of the field behind a batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion is a vast number, as in 'their fans are legion', from the Roman army unit.

clue.text: Burger, and meal with it, prepared in hazardous area?

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been worked up from raw ingredients, so these letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A fast-food order of a burger and a meal, cooked up somewhere risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges BURGER, AND MEAL and IT together; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of Atlantic off Florida is famed in legend for ships and planes vanishing, so it is a perilous zone.

clue.text: Uncomfortable week in a hospital room

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for week inside the phrase a ward

parts.note: a ward is a room of beds in a hospital

explanation.surface: A patient spends a miserable week stuck on a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling ill at ease or embarrassed is a common synonym, as in an awkward silence.

clue.text: Make matters worse? One left out cash!

indicators.note: out says one of the letters is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: to cap it all is to make a bad situation worse still
one L, L being the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Someone complains that leaving out the money is making things even worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'cap it all' loses one of its two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is money available for investment, a synonym for funds or cash.

clue.text: Border secured in record time, but it won't last

indicators.note: secured in means the edging word is fixed inside the record and the time

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
an era is a period of time
a hem is the folded border of a garment

explanation.surface: A sewing note: the trim is fastened for a record time, though it will not hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera are things that are short-lived, like flyers and tickets made to be thrown away.

clue.text: The King's power when allied with the Spanish

indicators.note: when allied with joins the Spanish article to the power word, side by side

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
vis is Latin for force or power

explanation.surface: A monarch's might is boosted by an alliance with Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The King is the nickname of Presley, the rock and roll singer.

clue.text: Success, then edge lost by crime writer

parts.note: joy means success, as in 'any joy with that?'

indicators.note: lost by says the edging word goes missing from the word crime

parts.note: a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A crime novelist finds success, then loses their edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crime writer' looks like the definition, but only 'writer' defines; CRIME loses RIM to leave CE.
explanation.definitionFit: James Joyce was the Irish author of Ulysses and Dubliners.

clue.text: Woman educated in Irish books causes trouble

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for a noun: the answer is a thing that causes trouble

indicators.note: in puts the woman's name inside the Irish and books abbreviations

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books
Educating Rita is the play and film, so the educated woman is Rita

explanation.surface: A woman who studied Irish literature is making a nuisance of herself.
explanation.definitionFit: An irritant is anything that annoys or inflames, which is to say a source of bother.

clue.text: By it one develops feeling for character

definitions.text: By it one develops feeling for character

parts.words: By it one develops feeling for character
parts.note: reads like learning empathy, but the feeling is touch and the characters are raised letters

explanation.surface: A way of building a sense of empathy for other people.
explanation.definitionFit: The system of raised dots lets blind readers recognise each letter by touch with their fingertips.

clue.text: Revolutionary facing little man presenting military insignia

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
V for versus, against or facing
Ron is a short form of the name Ronald

explanation.surface: A rebel squares up to a small fellow wearing army badges.
explanation.definitionFit: A V-shaped stripe on a sleeve shows a soldier's rank, a kind of military badge.

clue.text: Crude and rude depiction as thus

indicators.note: rude in the sense of rough and unworked, so the letters are left in a raw new order

explanation.surface: A rough, vulgar picture described as such.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rude' rearranges DEPICTION AS THUS; 'and' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude in the sense of unrefined or lacking finesse is a synonym.

clue.text: Vergers leaving church and parking in part of Oxford?

indicators.note: read as verges, the outer edges, going away, so the church word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a minster is a large church, such as York Minster
P is the standard map sign for parking

explanation.surface: Church officials leave a service and park somewhere in the university city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vergers' looks like church officials, but read it as things at the verges: MINSTER loses M and R, leaving INSTE. 'Oxford' is a lace-up shoe, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a laced shoe, and the arched middle part of a shoe is called that.

clue.text: Rider in old poetry recalled miners seizing day

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the poetry word runs backwards

parts.note: the Edda is a collection of Old Norse poems

indicators.note: seizing means the miners' union grabs the day abbreviation inside it

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers

explanation.surface: Ancient verse brought back to mind as miners seize the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' looks like a horseman; here it is a clause added to a document. NUM is Britain's miners' union.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a supplementary clause attached to a bill or contract, an addition.

clue.text: Animal in ancient times aboard ark?

indicators.note: aboard puts the dating abbreviation on board the vessel

parts.note: an ark is a boat, like Noah's
BC, before Christ, dates ancient times

explanation.surface: A creature that went on to Noah's Ark long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The bobcat is a North American wild cat, a member of the lynx family.

clue.text: Union assistance after hit show losing pounds

parts.note: to strike is to hit

indicators.note: losing says the pounds abbreviation drops out of the show word

parts.note: a play is a stage show
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: A hit show is losing money and needs help from the union.
explanation.definitionFit: Money a trade union gives its members while they are on strike is union support.

clue.text: Campaign pressing South Africa on journalist rejected

parts.note: a cru is a wine of a particular vineyard, the product of a pressing of grapes

indicators.note: rejected means the journalist abbreviation is turned back

parts.note: ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: An urgent campaign in South Africa about a reporter who was turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pressing' looks like urgent; it is a wine, CRU. 'on' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade is a vigorous campaign for a cause, such as one against corruption.

clue.text: Butter potentially that's no good sent out from Blighty

definitions.note: a butter here is something that butts with its horns

indicators.note: sent out from says the no-good letters are expelled from the country

parts.note: Blighty is old British slang for England, the homeland

explanation.surface: Butter that has gone off is sent away from Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Butter is not the dairy spread but a thing that butts: a horned antelope may well butt.
explanation.definitionFit: An African antelope with spiral horns could charge with its head, so it is a potential butter.

clue.text: Test regularly applied for instance

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word applied

explanation.surface: A test that is set at regular intervals, for instance.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a case in point, which is a synonym for a specimen of something.

clue.text: Bar from acting otherwise

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the phrase acting otherwise

explanation.surface: An actor is banned from performing any other way.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a bar of cast metal, such as gold.

clue.text: Provocation on steamship is not desired

parts.note: needle is provocation, ill feeling, as in a needle match

explanation.surface: Nobody wants trouble stirred up aboard the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unnecessary is not wanted or required, so the senses match.

clue.text: Member with seat taking no active role

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
a chair is a seat

explanation.surface: A committee member keeps a seat but does nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic or general comments from the sidelines without taking part.

clue.text: Last couple escaping death in Great Plague

indicators.note: in puts the shortened death word inside the great word

parts.note: epic means great or heroic in scale

indicators.note: the last two letters of the death word get away

parts.note: demise is a formal word for death

explanation.surface: Two people at the end flee from death during the Great Plague of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is a widespread outbreak of disease, which is an epidemic.

clue.text: TV Edna — here topless — might be honoured

indicators.note: might be says these letters could become something else when rearranged
topless says the word here loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A television star called Edna, appearing topless, might be given an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' turns HERE into ERE; 'might be' rearranges TVEDNA with ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be venerated is to be revered or held in deep respect.

clue.text: Country club entertainer and singles keeping fit

parts.note: a DJ plays records in a nightclub

indicators.note: keeping means the two single letters hold the fit word between them

parts.note: I is one, so singles are two I's
a bout is a fit, as of coughing

explanation.surface: A country club hires an entertainer, while single members stay in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Djibouti is a small nation in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Closed section different outside boundary

indicators.note: outside means the different word goes round the boundary word

parts.note: else means other or different, as in someone else
a lip is an edge or boundary

explanation.surface: A sealed-off area beyond a different border.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the conic sections, an oval is the closed curve, unlike the parabola and hyperbola.

clue.text: Something sweet, a small volume, consumed by elder?

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed inside the elder word

parts.note: an elder is a kind of tree
CL, a centilitre, is a small volume

explanation.surface: A little measure of a sweet thing is drunk by an older person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elder' looks like an older person; it is the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick dark syrup from sugar refining is a sweet substance.

clue.text: Wreath for head maenad in frenzy

indicators.note: in frenzy means the word maenad is thrown wildly about

explanation.surface: A wild Bacchic woman in a frenzy wears garlands on her head.
explanation.definitionFit: An anadem is a garland or chaplet worn on the head, a poetic word.

clue.text: Family members up in church recess

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the family words run upwards, reversed

parts.note: a sister (sis) and father (pa) are members of a family

explanation.surface: Relatives climb up into an alcove in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An apsis is a variant of apse, the vaulted recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: Recording traps loving couple, not married, summoned to court

indicators.note: traps means the recording holds the couple word inside it

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc recording

indicators.note: not says the married abbreviation is removed from the couple word

parts.note: a couple who are an item are romantically linked

explanation.surface: A tape catches an unmarried couple, who are then called to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cited in law has been ordered to appear before a judge.
